headline.headline: METS SAVAGE REDS, 9-1, AS SOTO AND CREW ERUPT FOR FIVE IN FIFTH
headline.deck: New York pours it on in Cincinnati, scoring in three separate innings to cruise
headline.body:
CINCINNATI -- The New York Mets turned Great American Ball Park into a house of horrors for the hometown Reds on Wednesday night, scoring nine runs on the strength of a four-run third inning and a devastating four-run fifth to walk away with a 9-1 victory before 27,207 fans. Juan Soto provided extra-base punch with a double, and the Mets kept the pressure building through eight innings of methodical, relentless offense that left the Reds thoroughly outclassed.

Cincinnati managed its lone run in the third inning and offered nothing else of consequence the rest of the night. McLean hit Arroyo with a pitch, a small footnote in what became a thoroughly one-sided evening. The Mets added two more insurance runs in the eighth to complete the rout, finishing the game in a crisp two hours and 29 minutes.

Doubles from Soto, Ewing, Stewart, and Lowe provided the extra-base architecture for a New York lineup that found holes all night against a Cincinnati pitching staff that simply had no answers. The Mets, riding high in the NL East race, showed Wednesday exactly why they are among the National League's most dangerous clubs heading into the summer stretch.

secondary.headline: ROYALS RIDE THREE HOME RUNS PAST NATIONALS, 6-2
secondary.deck: Jensen, Thomas, and Massey go deep as Kansas City builds lead through six innings
secondary.body:
WASHINGTON -- Kansas City needed only three home runs and an early lead to dispatch the Washington Nationals, 6-2, at Nationals Park on Wednesday. Quinton Jensen launched his ninth homer of the season, Lane Thomas added his fifth, and Michael Massey connected for his seventh as the Royals built a 6-0 advantage through six innings before Washington managed to answer with two runs in the bottom of the sixth.

The Royals scored in each of the first three innings, establishing control from the opening pitch and never surrendering the lead. Josh Mead was hit by a pitch from Alex Lange, but it barely registered in a game Kansas City controlled wire to wire. The final was 6-2, the game completed in two hours and 49 minutes before a modest crowd of 17,643.

secondary.headline: TRAE YOUNG TO DECLINE $49M OPTION, LEAVING WIZARDS IN LIMBO
secondary.deck: Washington's star guard set to become a free agent as rebuilding franchise faces uncertain summer
secondary.body:
WASHINGTON -- Trae Young plans to decline his $48.97 million player option for the 2026-27 season, according to sources, setting the stage for one of the most consequential free agency decisions of the summer. Young's departure would leave the Washington Wizards, already deep in a rebuilding project, without their marquee offensive talent heading into next season.

The news arrives just as the NBA's conference semifinals continue and the Knicks are still celebrating their first championship in 53 years. Owner James Dolan told WFAN on Wednesday that he will not push New York into the second apron to preserve the roster, a declaration that signals fiscal restraint even in the wake of a title. Young's next destination figures to reshape the Eastern Conference balance of power before training camps open in the fall.

secondary.headline: GIANTS STUN BRAVES IN ATLANTA, 7-2, BEHIND BALDWIN'S 14TH BLAST
secondary.deck: San Francisco overcomes early deficit and a weather delay to hand Atlanta a rare home loss
secondary.body:
ATLANTA -- The San Francisco Giants survived a one hour and 52 minute weather delay and spotted the Atlanta Braves a first-inning lead before roaring back to win 7-2 at Truist Park on Wednesday. Colton Baldwin cracked his 14th home run of the season, Willy Adames connected for his 12th, and Ji-Hwan Bae added a long ball as starter Grant Holmes earned the win to improve San Francisco's chances in the NL West.

Rafael Devers hit his 10th home run for the Braves and Jung Hoo Lee added his fourth, but Atlanta's offense stalled after the first inning and the Giants outscored them 6-0 from the second inning onward. Luis Arrayz contributed a double among the extra-base hits for San Francisco, which now carries momentum into Thursday's rematch against the first-place Braves. The game drew 31,266 to Truist Park and finished in two hours and 41 minutes of playing time.

column.headline: DOLAN'S WALLET SNAPS SHUT JUST AS THE KNICKS REACH THE TOP
column.body:
New York waited 53 years for a championship, and the champagne had barely dried before James Dolan stepped to the microphone at WFAN to announce he would not spend into the second apron to keep the winning roster together. That is the Knicks' luck in a single sentence. The city earns its crown and the owner immediately signals that the celebration has a price ceiling. It is familiar, it is frustrating, and Knicks fans know better than to be surprised.

Meanwhile, Trae Young is looking at a $48.97 million option and deciding to walk away from it, which tells you everything about how much he believes in what the open market will offer. If Young lands somewhere with legitimate playoff infrastructure, the Eastern Conference picture shifts in a hurry. The Knicks just won it all. Whether they can stay there depends on decisions being made right now, in offices and on phones, by men who may not be thinking as boldly as this moment demands.

story.headline: MARLINS BATTER PHILLIES IN PHILLY, ROLL TO 12-4 ROUT BEFORE 37,000
story.deck: Miami erupts for four runs in second, four more in sixth to overwhelm Philadelphia
story.body:
PHILADELPHIA — The Miami Marlins turned Citizens Bank Park into their personal batting cage Wednesday night, pounding the Philadelphia Phillies 12-4 before a crowd of 37,591 that grew quieter with each passing inning. Miami struck for four runs in the second inning and four more in the sixth, sending the Phillies to a lopsided defeat that was never seriously in doubt after the third frame.

Kyle Stowers and Owen Caissie each went deep for their seventh home runs of the season, while Nate Marsee added his fourth and Connor Mack his third — Mack was also hit by a Kerkering pitch during the evening. A wild pitch by Mayza did not dent Miami's momentum, as the Marlins finished with 12 runs on the strength of extra-base contributions from Stowers, Vidal Brujan Ruiz, and Trea Turner, who also swiped a bag alongside Bryson Stott. Philadelphia stranded a staggering 19 runners, leaving opportunity after opportunity to rot on the basepaths.

The loss continued a troubling pattern for a Phillies club that could not convert traffic into runs, going 1-for-what-felt-like-everything with runners in scoring position. Miami's victory was the most emphatic result of a full Wednesday slate that also featured the New York Mets crushing Cincinnati 9-1, the San Francisco Giants topping Atlanta 7-2, and the Los Angeles Dodgers edging Tampa Bay 5-4 on Freddie Freeman's 12th home run of the year.

story.headline: DOLAN DRAWS THE LINE AS TRAE YOUNG EYES THE DOOR
story.deck: Knicks owner vows to stay under second apron while Young prepares to bolt Washington.
story.body:
The confetti from the Knicks' first NBA championship since 1973 has barely been swept off Madison Square Garden's hardwood, and already the business of basketball is threatening to complicate the celebration. Owner James Dolan told WFAN radio Wednesday that he will not push the franchise into the second apron to keep the championship roster together, a financial boundary that could force the front office into painful decisions about which title contributors return next season.

Meanwhile, across the league, the summer's most consequential free agency drama is taking shape in Washington. Wizards star Trae Young is expected to decline his $48.97 million player option for the 2026-27 season, according to sources, making the five-time All-Star point guard the biggest name on the open market. Young, who was dealt from Atlanta to Washington two years ago, never fully committed to a long-term future with the rebuilding Wizards, and his imminent departure leaves the franchise searching for a new direction.

The news arrives against a backdrop of NBA nostalgia, as LeBron James, Kevin Love and other members of Cleveland's legendary 2016 championship squad reunited in the United Kingdom this week to mark the tenth anniversary of their historic title. That reunion, combined with Ben Stiller's newly announced Knicks documentary project with A24 and HBO, underscored a league caught between celebrating its past and bracing for a seismic summer of roster upheaval.

story.headline: GOLDEN KNIGHTS ROLL THE DICE ON AHL COACH RYAN CRAIG AS NEXT HEAD MAN
story.deck: Vegas stuns hockey world by promoting minor-league bench boss to lead NHL club
story.body:
LAS VEGAS — The Vegas Golden Knights made one of the most surprising front-office moves of the offseason Wednesday, promoting Ryan Craig from head coach of their AHL affiliate to lead the NHL club, a decision that left veteran observers scratching their heads. Craig, who built his reputation guiding the Henderson Silver Knights in the minors, now inherits one of the league's most pressure-packed benches with no prior NHL head coaching experience at the top level. Former ESPN analyst Michael Wilbon was among the most vocal critics, calling the hire baffling and questioning why the organization would bypass established candidates with proven big-league track records.

The move caps a turbulent stretch for Vegas, which parted ways with its previous bench boss before the ink had dried on the offseason calendar. Craig, a former NHL forward who played parts of several seasons with Tampa Bay and other clubs, earned respect as a player developer in Henderson but faces an immediate credibility test with a Golden Knights locker room accustomed to Stanley Cup expectations. General manager Kelly McCrimmon did not hold a formal press conference, leaving reporters and fans alike to parse a brief organizational statement.

Elsewhere around the league, the Nashville Predators continued their own front-office reconstruction Thursday, announcing that veteran forward Jamie Langenbrunner has been hired as a special assistant to new general manager Chris MacFarland. Meanwhile, the Buffalo Sabres acquired the No. 20 overall pick in next week's NHL Draft from San Jose, surrendering defenseman Michael Kesselring in the deal, as Buffalo aggressively positions itself to add blue-chip talent ahead of what the franchise hopes will be a long-awaited competitive window.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS TEAMS RETOOL FOR 2026 CAMPAIGN
story.deck: Three franchises make bold moves at signal-caller as the offseason market heats up.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has erupted into a full-blown quarterback frenzy, with the Las Vegas Raiders, Cleveland Browns, and New Orleans Saints all making significant moves at the position in recent weeks. Las Vegas struck first, agreeing to terms with veteran passer Sam Darnold on a two-year, $58 million deal, banking on the journeyman's resurgent 2025 campaign to anchor a rebuilt offense under new head coach Mike Vrabel. Cleveland, still searching for stability under center since the Deshaun Watson era collapsed, moved aggressively to acquire Jacksonville Jaguars backup Mac Jones in a trade that sent a third-round pick to Florida.

The Saints made the most eyebrow-raising move of the spring, trading up in the 2026 NFL Draft to select Oregon quarterback Dante Carver with the fifth overall pick, signaling a full commitment to youth after two disappointing seasons from the Derek Carr era. New Orleans general manager Mickey Loomis called Carver the most polished pocket passer to enter the draft since Bryce Young, a bold proclamation that drew immediate scrutiny from analysts. Carver threw for 4,312 yards and 38 touchdowns in his final college season, earning Pac-12 Offensive Player of the Year honors.

Elsewhere around the league, the Dallas Cowboys parted ways with wide receiver CeeDee Lamb following a contract dispute that stretched through the winter, with Lamb quickly landing a four-year, $132 million extension with the Philadelphia Eagles. The move sent shockwaves through the NFC East, further fortifying an Eagles roster that already boasts one of the conference's most dangerous offenses heading into training camp. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones called the split painful but necessary, insisting Dallas would find its next playmaker through June's supplemental draft process or via remaining free agency options.
